business_summary: Tesla, Inc. is classed in the Automobiles sector. The evidence supplied has no business description or company documents, so this summary uses only financial figures: FY25 operating margin of 9.9%, FY25 net profit of USD 3,794 million, and borrowings of 0.1x equity.
why_own: The case rests on a profitable, lightly indebted company (no loss-making quarters in the last four, debt/equity of 0.1x) whose 5-year revenue CAGR of 24.63% has slowed to 5.19% over 3 years while net profit has fallen. The evidence is thin, with no results or call documents, so there are no qualitative drivers. At a trailing P/E of 459x and a price/book of 17.98x, the price already assumes a lot.

drivers.statement: Operating margin holds near high single digits. It is 9.9% in FY25, down 9.84 percentage points over three years, so further erosion would undermine the case.
Revenue keeps growing. The 3-year CAGR is 5.19%, well below the 5-year CAGR of 24.63%, so stalling growth is the thing to watch. (warn line tightened by code from 3 to 3.63.)
The balance sheet stays conservative. Debt/equity is 0.1x and interest cover is 16.62x. (warn line tightened by code from 0.3 to 0.13.)
Returns on capital stay positive and do not fall further. ROCE is 6.22% and ROE is 4.89%, both low in absolute terms.
Return on equity should stay above 10%. (added by code: currently 4.89.)
Trailing P/E should stay below 60x, or the price needs years of flawless growth. (added by code: currently 459.04.)
Revenue in the latest quarter should not fall year on year. (added by code: currently -0.17.)
Net profit in the latest quarter should not fall more than 25% year on year. (added by code: currently -42.68.)

kill_criteria.description: Operating margin falls below 5%, which would leave little cushion on the current profit base.
More than 2 of the last 4 quarters are loss-making.

risks.statement: Valuation is very demanding. The trailing P/E is 459x and price/book is 17.98x, so any earnings disappointment could matter a lot. There is no own-history P/E comparison available.

Profits are shrinking. Net profit growth is -32.9% a year over 3 years, and trailing 4-quarter net profit of USD 3,218 million is below FY25's USD 3,794 million. The reasons are not covered by the evidence and remain untested.
Margins and returns are thin for the valuation. Operating margin is down 9.84 percentage points in 3 years to 9.9%, and ROCE is 6.22%.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis rests on a clean balance sheet, but nothing in the evidence supports the price. P/E is 459x and the market-implied 10-year profit growth is 51.91% a year, against -32.9% delivered over 3 years. Latest-quarter revenue is -0.17% and profit -42.68% year on year, so the slowdown is continuing. The kill lines are lenient: a margin of 5% or a ROCE of 3% would each be a collapse before anything trips. The thesis is wrong if profit keeps shrinking while the multiple holds, because no evidence supplied shows what would reverse the decline. What would change this view: Two consecutive quarters of year-on-year profit growth, with operating margin stable at or above 9.9%, would remove the objection that earnings are still shrinking.
